questions.q: What did Joshua do before he could begin his minimalist journey?
a: Spent two years paying off all his debt
Sold his house and moved abroad
Quit his job to travel the world
Gave away most of his possessions
questions.why: Lesson 1 says he went two years without vacations, eating out or luxuries to clear his debt.

questions.q: What do the letters in the TARA method stand for?
a: Tolerate, accept, respect, appreciate
Trust, ask, reflect, act
Talk, agree, resolve, adjust
Try, allow, revise, approve
questions.why: Lesson 2 lays out the four steps for accepting other people's quirks and interests.

questions.q: What is the TARA method meant to help you do?
a: Accept people who do not share your values
Persuade friends to try minimalism
Sort your possessions into four piles
Track your spending each month
questions.why: Lesson 2 says it is healthier to change how you deal with others than to change them.

questions.q: What does the summary say about your job in relation to your identity?
a: It is just one part of a complex person
It should define who you are
It can never be changed once chosen
It matters less than your possessions
questions.why: Lesson 3 says a job is just a job and you are a complex person with many passions.

questions.q: What does the summary suggest asking people instead of what they do for a living?
a: What they are passionate about
How much money they earn
Where they grew up
What they studied at school
questions.why: Lesson 3 says this seeds more meaningful conversations and better stories.
